title: Readability & Accessibility Audit
useCase: Check plain language, accessibility, and global English
promptText:
You are a technical editor specializing in plain language and accessibility. Audit the document below against these criteria:

Document:
<document>
<mark>[PASTE DOCUMENT HERE]</mark>
</document>

Audit criteria:
- Readability: flag sentences over 25 words; identify passive voice; highlight unnecessary jargon
- Global English: flag idioms, metaphors, and culturally specific references that will not translate well
- Accessibility: identify spatial language ("see above", "click the icon on the left"), color-only instructions, and non-descriptive links ("click here")
- Inclusivity: flag gendered language; suggest gender-neutral alternatives

Output format:
- One table per criterion
- Columns: Original text | Issue | Suggested fix
- End with a summary paragraph of the 3 highest-priority improvements

title: Generate Alt Text for Blog Visuals & Infographics
useCase: Write accessibility-compliant (WCAG 2.2) and SEO-friendly alt text for photos, diagrams, and illustrations
promptText:
You are a digital accessibility (a11y) specialist and SEO content strategist.

Create alternative text (alt text) for an image used in a blog post or web article.

Image & Context Details:
- Image description or paste/upload: <mark>[DESCRIBE THE IMAGE IN DETAIL OR PASTE AN IMAGE UPLOAD]</mark>
- Article title & topic context: <mark>[ARTICLE TITLE AND WHAT SECTION THIS IMAGE APPEARS IN]</mark>
- Image type: <mark>[e.g., Photograph / Conceptual Illustration / Workflow Diagram / Infographic / Chart / Meme]</mark>
- Target SEO keyword (optional): <mark>[KEYWORD IF RELEVANT, OR 'None']</mark>

Guidelines (WCAG 2.2 Standards):
1. Do not start with redundant phrases like "Image of", "Photo of", or "Graphic showing". Screen readers announce graphics automatically.
2. Convey the functional purpose and informational meaning, not just visual decoration.
3. If the image contains text, flowcharts, or data points, include the essential text and data trends.
4. Keep standard alt text between 80 to 125 characters whenever possible.
5. If the image is purely decorative, note that an empty alt attribute (alt="") should be used.

Output Deliverables:
1. Standard Alt Text: Single concise sentence (<125 characters) ideal for the HTML `alt` attribute.
2. Long Description (if image is a chart, workflow diagram, or data infographic): Markdown breakdown summarizing all steps or data values for screen readers.
3. Suggested Editorial Caption: 1 reader-facing caption to display below the image for visual context.

promptText:

- Preferred channel: <mark>[e.g., Email, Slack/Teams message, Talking points for a 1-on-1 meeting]</mark>

4. Use collaborative "we" for solutions, but clear "I" statements for personal observations.

- Section 1: Written Message (ready to send via chosen channel).
- Section 2: 3 anticipated objections and how to calmly respond in real time.

- Core objective: <mark>[WHAT ARE YOU TRYING TO CONVINCE THEM TO DO OR BELIEVE?]</mark>

4. The "Steel-Manned" Refinement: How can I adjust or reframe the core argument to proactively inoculate against these criticisms without weakening my thesis?
